fatal_errors: The proposed NiTi material and martensitic transformation mechanism do not reconstruct the target study of FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived single crystals governed by solid-solution glide resistance, cryogenic dislocation inertia, and high-temperature Portevin-Le Chatelier pinning.

The response conflates reversible martensite variant reorientation and transformation strain with plastic deformation; these processes can produce recoverable inelastic strain and should be separated from irreversible dislocation plasticity.

Describing low-temperature martensitic NiTi as exhibiting typical pseudoelastic behavior is generally inconsistent: conventional superelasticity occurs when austenite is mechanically transformed above the austenite-finish temperature.
explanation: NiTi is a scientifically plausible material for studying temperature-dependent mechanical behavior, and the proposed temperature-controlled loading with in situ phase measurements is reasonably falsifiable. However, it is not an evidence-supported reconstruction of the hidden target: it changes the alloy system, initial crystal state, loading geometry, temperature range, measured quantity, and all central mechanisms. It omits CRSS measurements, low-temperature phonon-drag/inertial dulling, MSAD-based solid-solution strengthening, high-temperature serrated flow, Cottrell versus Suzuki segregation tests, and composition-dependent Mn/Fe and Cr trends. The hypothesis also needs sharper terminology distinguishing recoverable transformation strain from true plastic deformation and provides no cited evidence or quantitative predictions.
